tools.name: calendar_events_list
tools.description: Returns events on the specified calendar. (GET /calendars/{calendarId}/events)

calendar_id.description: Calendar identifier. To retrieve calendar IDs call the calendarList.list method.

time_min.description: Lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time to filter by. Must be an RFC3339 timestamp, e.g. 2026-01-19T00:00:00Z.

time_max.description: Upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time to filter by. Must be an RFC3339 timestamp.

q.description: Free text search terms to find events that match these terms in the summary, description, location, or attendees' emails and display names.

single_events.description: Whether to expand recurring events into instances and only return single one-off events and instances of recurring events, but not the underlying recurring events themselves. Default False.

show_deleted.description: Whether to include deleted events (with status equal to 'cancelled') in the result. Default False.

max_results.description: Maximum number of events returned on one result page. Default 30.

tools.name: calendar_events_get
tools.description: Returns an event based on its Google Calendar ID. (GET /calendars/{calendarId}/events/{eventId})

calendar_id.description: Calendar identifier. To retrieve calendar IDs call the calendarList.list method.

tools.custom_source:
def calendar_events_get(db_path='state.db', **kwargs):
    """Returns an event based on its Google Calendar ID. (GET /calendars/{calendarId}/events/{eventId})"""
    _missing = [p for p in ['calendar_id', 'event_id'] if kwargs.get(p) is None]
    if _missing:
        return {'error': 'missing required parameters: ' + ', '.join(_missing), 'status': 400}
    import sqlite3, json, datetime, hashlib
    try:
        _eid = int(kwargs['event_id'])
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return {'error': 'invalid event_id: %r' % (kwargs.get('event_id'),), 'status': 400}
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    cur = conn.cursor()
    try:
        row = cur.execute(
            'SELECT e."id", e."title", e."event_date", e."created_at", d.* FROM "agent_events" e '
            'JOIN "cal_event_details" d ON d."event_id" = e."id" WHERE e."id" = ? AND d."calendar_id" = ?',
            [_eid, str(kwargs['calendar_id'])]).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return {'error': 'event not found', 'status': 404}
        att = cur.execute('SELECT * FROM "cal_event_attendees" WHERE "event_id" = ? ORDER BY "id"', [_eid]).fetchall()
        out = {
            'kind': 'calendar#event',
            'id': row['id'],
            'status': row['status'],
            'summary': row['title'],
            'description': row['description'],
            'location': row['location'],
            'color_id': row['color_id'],
            'transparency': row['transparency'],
            'visibility': row['visibility'],
            'organizer': {'email': row['organizer_email']},
            'start': {'date_time': row['start_datetime'], 'time_zone': row['time_zone']},
            'end': {'date_time': row['end_datetime'], 'time_zone': row['time_zone']},
            'created': row['created_at'],
            'updated': row['updated'],
            'attendees': [
                {'email': a['email'], 'display_name': a['display_name'], 'response_status': a['response_status'],
                 'optional': bool(a['optional']), 'organizer': bool(a['organizer'])}
                for a in att
            ],
        }
        if row['recurrence']:
            out['recurrence'] = [row['recurrence']]
        return out
    finally:
        conn.close()

tools.name: calendar_events_insert

calendar_id.description: Calendar identifier. To retrieve calendar IDs call the calendarList.list method.

description.description: Description of the event. Can contain HTML.

location.description: Geographic location of the event as free-form text.

start.description: The (inclusive) start time of the event: object with 'date_time' (RFC3339 timestamp) or 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD, for all-day events), and optional 'time_zone' (IANA Time Zone Database name).

end.description: The (exclusive) end time of the event: object with 'date_time' (RFC3339 timestamp) or 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD, for all-day events), and optional 'time_zone'.

attendees.description: The attendees of the event: JSON list of objects, each with 'email' (required), and optional 'display_name', 'optional' (boolean), 'response_status' ('needsAction', 'declined', 'tentative', 'accepted').

recurrence.description: List of RRULE lines for a recurring event, as specified in RFC5545, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=4"]. Supported: FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY with INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL.

color_id.description: The color of the event. This is an ID referring to an entry in the event section of the colors definition (see the colors endpoint).

transparency.description: Whether the event blocks time on the calendar. 'opaque' (default) — the event does block time; 'transparent' — the event does not block time.

send_updates.description: Whether to send notifications about the creation of the new event. Acceptable values: 'all', 'externalOnly', 'none'. No mail is actually delivered in this sandbox; the value is validated only.

tools.name: calendar_freebusy_query
tools.description: Returns free/busy information for a set of calendars, computed from their non-transparent, non-cancelled events (recurring events are expanded). (POST /freeBusy)

time_min.description: The start of the interval for the query formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

time_max.description: The end of the interval for the query formatted as an RFC3339 timestamp.

items.description: List of calendars to query, as objects with an 'id' field, e.g. [{"id": "00000000000000000002"}]. Bare string IDs are also accepted.

time_zone.description: Time zone used in the response. Optional. The default is UTC; busy blocks are always reported in UTC in this sandbox.

role.description: The role assigned to the scope. Possible values: 'none', 'freeBusyReader', 'reader', 'writer', 'owner'.

scope.description: The extent to which calendar access is granted by this rule: object with 'type' ('default', 'user', 'group', or 'domain') and 'value' (the email address of a user or group, or the name of a domain; omitted for type 'default').

send_notifications.description: Whether to send notifications about the calendar sharing change. Optional. The default is True. No mail is delivered in this sandbox.
